div.head: IV Atr 4
div.ab: Et diximus: homo qui hamsocnam faciet intra portum sine licentia et summam infracturam aget de placito ungebendeo uel qui aliquem innocentem affliget in uia regia, si iaceat, iaceat in ungildan ækere.

Et diximus: homo qui hamsocnam faciet intra portum sine licentia et summam infracturam aget de placito ungebendeo, vel qui aliquem innocentem affliget in via regia, si iaceat, iaceat in ungildan ækere.

Und wir haben bestimmt: wer innerhalb der Stadt Angriff auf jemandes Heim ohne Erlaubniss ausführt oder schwerste Verletzung [königlichen Stadtfriedens] verübt an einem [von ihm noch] nicht zum Rechtsgang aufgeforderten[?], oder wer einen Unschuldigen auf der königlichen [Heer]strasse angreift, wenn er dabei getödtet wird, liege er in dem nicht [durch Wergeld] entgoltenen [unehrlichen] Felde.

And we have determined: whoever attacks someone's home within the town without permission, or commits the gravest breach [of the king's town-peace] against someone not [yet] summoned [by him] to legal process[?], or whoever attacks an innocent person on the king's highway, if he is killed in doing so, let him lie in the field that is not paid for [by wergild, i.e. dishonoured].

And we have decreed that a man who, within the town, makes forcible entry into another man's house without permission and commits a breach of the peace of the worst kind… and he who assaults an innocent parson on the king's highway, if he is slain, shall lie in an unhonoured grave.
div.note: ‘ungebendeo’ should perhaps be corrected to ‘rihtes ungebedene’ (Liebermann).
